## Configuration and first startup

Run `python3 tools/init_config.py` as the checkout owner. It creates missing split
files with independent random database/API/operator/backup credentials and grants
read ACLs to UID 7474. Existing files are never read or overwritten by this tool;
ACLs may be refreshed. Install the host `acl` package first. Bind files remain
owned by the operator, without world-read permission or root-owned bind mounts.
Existing volumes must already be owned by UID 7474; an administrator must migrate
older root-owned volumes from a verified backup before startup. Fresh named
volumes inherit the image directory ownership. Set `LIMES_OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
privately in `config/secrets.env`. Keep tokens out
of history, CLI arguments and logs. Use independent consumer, operator and backup
tokens. Back up configuration securely; it is untracked and excluded from images.

`settings.env` contains tuning; `models.env` contains initial catalogue-validated
pins; `secrets.env` contains credentials. Empty env values are unset. In containers,
`/data/models/models.env` overrides seed pins and atomic tool writes target this
named volume. Model reports use that directory. New worker processes reload pins;
API query contexts refresh pins on their next use. Existing explicit environment values override
file pins. Rootless Docker can administer the stack; any Docker administrator can
start/stop it, while use needs only HTTP credentials.

The base file publishes only `127.0.0.1:8000:8000`. Run base configuration explicitly
with `-f docker-compose.yml`; the auto-loaded development override mounts source
and enables API reload, and must not be used for releases. Use HTTPS termination
forwarding to loopback for remote clients, or an ordinary SSH loopback tunnel.
Keep database and backup-control ports private. The desktop prompts for a session
token; profiles carry names/URLs only. Backup requires the operator session token.

## Operations without Docker membership

Set `LIMES_REMOTE_URL` and `LIMES_OPERATOR_TOKEN` on the client, then run
`venv/bin/limes remote run COMMAND OPTIONS`. Remote mode loads no Neo4j credential
or server configuration. Only HTTPS or loopback HTTP may carry a credential;
redirects are refused. It prints the request UUID before submission. Save that UUID:
reuse `--request-id UUID` with the exact payload after an uncertain response rather
than issuing a new operation. `--no-wait` returns after submission. Resume observation
using `venv/bin/limes remote status UUID --wait`; disconnecting never cancels or
replays work. Output and status are operator-only. A timeout does not imply rollback.

| Command | Parameters |
|---|---|
| ingest | `--source ID` |
| ingest-all | none |
| backfill | `--source ID --days N` (1–36500) |
| reextract | `--version X.Y.Z`, optional `--source ID` |
| select-models | `--stage provisional` or `--stage measured` |
| evaluate | optional `--evaluation extraction`, `resolution` or `nl2cypher` |
| migrate | `--version X.Y.Z` |
| backup | none |
| stamp-embeddings | none |

Make operational targets call the same HTTP remote CLI; only `up`/`down` administer
Docker. `make select-models STAGE=measured` and `make evaluate EVALUATION=resolution`
replace the old arbitrary ARGS. Bootstrap structured sources first, stamp embeddings,
then start unstructured backfill. Real measurement can spend money and is an explicit
operator run. Automated verification uses mocked catalogue/inference and gold sets.

Backup returns the named dump only after database recovery. Transfer artifacts using
an administrator-owned volume backup process; the desktop never needs host shell
access to request a dump. Restore on an isolated stopped database with the matching
Neo4j image using `neo4j-admin database load neo4j --from-path=...`; replace the
application volume only after verifying the restored graph. Do not restore into a
running database or overwrite an operator archive as a test.

## Reproducible deployment and evidence

Review and commit changes before deployment. `python3 tools/deploy.py --check`
requires a clean checkout and fetches current main through the baseline guard.
`python3 tools/deploy.py` is an explicit administrator operation: builds from that
commit with full SHA image tags and OCI revision labels, validates non-root image
users, resolves immutable image IDs, starts the base topology with those IDs,
waits for service health, checks running images, and records revision/image IDs and
non-secret seed-config hashes in `deployments/SHA/RUN/record.json`. Configured proxy CA
trust is mounted during API/worker dependency builds in managed environments.

`GET /version` requires a bearer token and exposes the image revision even while
Neo4j is unavailable. Keep the deployment record outside Git with backups. Reuse
its images.yml with the base Compose file to restart the exact saved images; do
not substitute a mutable tag or load the development override. Container image
IDs record the actual artifacts even when an upstream base-image tag later moves.
Archive those images or publish them by digest to retain rebuild/rollback artifacts.
Mutable volumes are intentionally separate from image versioning; pin/evaluation
reports record their own version keys. Redeploying an old image is not a schema
rollback; the ontology downgrade guard still applies.

No code-generation tool or test automatically deploys, tags, commits, pushes,
merges, touches production or makes paid calls. Historical test-instance facts
cannot establish a current release stamp; deploy records are created only by an
actual authorized deployment. CI records JUnit results for every required suite.

## News acquisition and scheduling (planned)

GDELT backfill accepts explicit windows of at most 96 fifteen-minute slots
(one day); larger requests fail before network access and must be split into
consecutive jobs. Compressed responses are capped at 16 MiB, decompressed exports
at 128 MiB and rows at 250,000. Malformed/partial records block checkpoint
advancement; successful checkpoints use the covered window endpoint and never
move backward. Failed document loads remain replayable; reextract bypasses the
cache and retracts only extracted evidence after replacement loading succeeds.
No production ingestion is implied by the disposable fixture scenario.

Agency acquisition remains within the existing worker's operator jobs; no
standalone utility or additional service is planned. Provider access/retention
terms, bounded acquisition, per-channel checkpoints and retry behavior must be
settled before unattended ingestion. An external timer may later submit the same
authenticated HTTP jobs, reuse request UUIDs after uncertain responses, observe
completion and avoid overlapping runs. This is planned operational guidance,
not an installed scheduler. Current legacy budget flags are ignored; job timeout
is not a monetary spending cap. Cheap filtering and explicit work limits are
future requirements in [ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md).
